componentAcceptance: A dedicated real remote-write flow now covers T15 artifact cleanup. After a successful write, the produced file is deleted and the same request is submitted again. The original succeeded Task/operation is returned with one fs_write and one operation row, and the file is not recreated. Changed content still raises TASK_REQUEST_CONFLICT. Native journal dedup also survives fresh connections and archived runs.
productAcceptance: T15 passes at integration level: same operation ID plus same digest returns the original record, altered digest conflicts and dedup survives artifact cleanup. Dedup does not restore or roll back artifacts. Formal scores are 0/20 work packages, 8/63 scenarios and M0 11/12.
testRuns: remote-write including the new artifact-cleanup dedup case: 15 tests / 15 pass / 0 fail.
node scripts/integration-task-probe.mjs: 29 tests / 29 pass / 0 fail with verified SQLite driver.
Final npm test: phase one 1590/1586/0/4 and phase two 371/288/0/83; total 1960 tests, 1875 pass, 0 fail, 83 skipped.
limitations: The test proves identity dedup after artifact deletion, not artifact restoration, rollback or garbage collection semantics.
No real model inference, production process, push or release was used.
